items.title: Boeing Lands $131 Bil F-15 Fighter Jet Contract, Analyst Lifts Booz Allen Targets
items.summary: Boeing wins $131 bil F-15 fighter jet contract. Parsons, General Dynamics win DOD awards. William Blair lifts Booz Allen targets on acquisition.

items.title: Is Textron Benefiting from the Growing Demand for Light Jets?
items.summary: TXT's 500th Citation CJ4 delivery and upcoming CJ4 Gen3 highlight its push to capture demand for efficient, versatile light business jets.

items.title: Boeing Is Delivering Airplanes Faster Than It Is Delivering Cash
items.summary: The planemaker's delivery recovery is real, and the cash it throws off is still a small fraction of the annual figure management says is well within reach.

items.title: General Dynamics Stock: Is Wall Street Bullish or Bearish?
items.summary: Although General Dynamics has outperformed the broader market over the past year, Wall Street analysts maintain a cautiously optimistic outlook on the stock’s prospects.

items.title: Can HII Benefit From Growing Demand for Submarine Construction?
items.summary: Huntington Ingalls is poised to benefit from rising U.S. Navy submarine demand, backed by major Columbia and Virginia-class roles and shipyard investments.

items.title: RTX, Lockheed, and 7 More Stocks to Consider as Missile Production Rockets Higher
items.summary: Coming into Tuesday trading, shares of 10 major defense contractors Barron’s looked at—including  Lockheed Martin Northrop Grumman Huntington-Ingalls Industries  and others—were down an average of 17% since fighting started in Iran.  Only  RTX  and  General Dynamics  were up.  U.S. defense spending is at a record high, European defense spending is growing, and the Iran war is teaching the American military how to build more autonomous weapons systems and smart munitions.

items.title: RTX Stock Gets a Radar Lock on a $23B Navy Win
items.summary: RTX Corporation secured a $22.9 billion Navy Tomahawk contract and topped Q2 2026 earnings estimates, prompting raised full-year guidance and continued dividend growth.

items.title: General Dynamics (GD) Stock Looks Reasonable After Its 119% Five Year Run
items.summary: General Dynamics stock has delivered a 119.4% total return over the past 5 years, yet current checks suggest it may still trade below an estimate of intrinsic value based on a Discounted Cash Flow (DCF) model and supporting market multiples. Recent headlines around new U.S. government contracts and operational issues at a Texas factory mean investors are weighing that valuation gap against execution and reputational risks. A 119.4% return over 5 years points to strong shareholder gains,...
